task.instruction: Choose exactly one indivisible package for this cycle—diagnosis, workflow readiness, or mapping automation—within six engineer-weeks and 60 operations-hours. Produce a resource-allocation note with owners, timing, and a decision trigger. Cite the supplied evidence IDs.

evidence.content: Of 73 suppliers, 31 stalled: 14 mapping, 9 legal, 8 missing documents; 7 had multiple blockers.
The cycle budget is six engineer-weeks and 60 operations-hours. Governance permits exactly one indivisible package; unused capacity cannot fund a second package.

Diagnosis costs one engineer-week and 60 operations-hours, samples 20 suppliers in ten days, and is reversible. Mapping automation costs five engineer-weeks and 20 operations-hours and addresses at most 14 stalls.
Readiness costs three engineer-weeks and 60 operations-hours, names an exception owner, sets a two-day SLA, and rehearses the runbook. Currently there is no owner or SLA; median response is 6.2 days.
A prior 48-partner intake had 20 stalls, missing reason tags, and 36 hours of manual triage.
A prior 55-partner intake had 17 mapping errors, no owner, and a four-week automation estimate.

nondiagnostic_target_a.content: 2026-04-16 — Decision: Spend 36 hours classifying the 20 partner stalls before building. Reason: Missing reason tags make the four-week estimate causally premature. Evidence: [rb-s1a-prior-01].
2026-05-14 — Decision: Assign an intake owner before addressing the 17 mapping errors. Reason: The absent owner makes exception response non-repeatable. Evidence: [rb-s1a-prior-02].

nondiagnostic_target_b.content: 2026-04-16 — Decision: Name a triage owner before sampling the 20 stalled partners. Reason: Accountability can stabilize intake while 36 hours remain available. Evidence: [rb-s1a-prior-01].
2026-05-14 — Decision: Sample ten mapping errors before committing four engineer-weeks. Reason: Seventeen errors do not establish one automatable cause. Evidence: [rb-s1a-prior-02].
